subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The Spartan Scytale
description: A fast breakdown of The Spartan Scytale for builders.

hook.text: Ancient Spartans wrapped leather strips around wooden rods to send secret military messages.

buildup.text: The scytale was a cylinder. You wrapped a strip of leather around it and wrote your message across the coils.

discovery.text: Unwound, the strip looked like random letters. Only a rod of the exact same diameter could decode it.

twist.text: The scytale is a transposition cipher — it scrambles letter order rather than replacing letters.

climax.text: Twenty-five centuries ago, Spartans understood that physical tools could protect information in transit.

punchline.text: A wooden stick. The first hardware encryption.

quiz.question: What type of cipher does the Spartan scytale use?
